sentence: The first card can be any of fifty-two, the next any of the rest.
claim: A standard deck has 52 cards; each position can take any card not yet used (52, then 51, then 50 ...).
source_title: Counting orders (permutations): n! (a textbook fact; link a stronger source, e.g. a probability text)
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. A counting rule, not a measurement. A person should replace the link with a textbook or encyclopedia page they trust.

sentence: Multiply all those choices, and you count the orders.
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Computed exactly by Python integers; anyone can check with a calculator that shows big integers.

sentence: The answer has sixty-eight digits, too big to say out loud.
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Computed.

sentence: Now give everyone alive a deck, eight billion of us.
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Not yet read (population.un.org was blocked when tried). The film says 'about eight billion' and shows 8.2 billion in the sum.

sentence: Shuffle once a second for fourteen billion years, the age of the universe.
claim: The universe began around 13.8 billion years ago ('fourteen billion' is a rounding; the sum uses 13.8).
source_title: NASA Science, Universe overview (history of the universe)
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. The page states 'Around 13.8 billion years ago, the universe expanded faster than the speed of light for a fraction of a second' (cosmic inflation, i.e. the start); it is a cosmologists' estimate.
builder_read: "Around 13.8 billion years ago, the universe expanded faster than the speed of light for a fraction of a second, a period called cosmic inflation."

sentence: Even then, you cover less than one part in a trillion trillion trillion of the orders.
claim: 8.2e9 people x 13.8e9 years x 3.156e7 s = 3.6e27 shuffles; 3.6e27 / 8.07e67 = 4.4e-41, which is less than 1 part in 10^36 (a trillion trillion trillion).
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Computed from c2, c4, c5. A thought experiment: every shuffle counted even if repeated.

sentence: Your shuffle is almost certainly the first of its kind.
claim: If a shuffle is fair and uniform, the chance that it matches any specific earlier one is 1 in 52!; against all 3.6e27 shuffles in the thought experiment it is 4.4e-41. (The chance that any two of those ever match is about 8e-14, by the birthday bound N^2 / (2 x 52!).)
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Probability statement, said as one ('almost certainly'). It assumes shuffles are fair and uniform; real shuffles are imperfect, so the film says 'shuffle well'.

sentence: Give the planet a thousand times more shufflers, and it barely changes.
claim: With 1,000 times the people the share is 4.4e-38: still less than 1 part in 10^36.
note: OPEN until a person opens the page. Computed.

sentence: Shuffle well, and your order has almost certainly never existed before.
